title: Retrieval-gated memory query selection
problem_solved: Avoid querying long-term memory on every turn when the current request does not justify retrieval.
responsibility_boundary: Own the pre-retrieval retrieve/skip decision and explicit query/reason handoff. It does not own memory stores, ranking, prompt assembly, durable writes, or downstream answer quality.

mechanism.summary: A bounded decision path receives the current message and emits retrieve/skip plus a search query and short reason. Downstream memory is queried only when retrieval is selected. If the gate itself cannot be trusted or executed, the source mechanism fails open to retrieval using the original message.
portable_obligations: declared failure behavior rather than silent retrieval suppression

replaceability: The original Waku gate, its model, prompt, memory stores, and Agent runtime are not privileged. Another deterministic or model-based mechanism may replace it if the selected case preserves the required decision/query/failure obligations and re-evaluates them.
reuse_preconditions: a case-specific retrieval policy and downstream store/query contract exist
the cost and false-positive consequences of retrieval are understood
the gate failure policy is explicitly chosen for the target case
decisions can be observed for later evaluation
known_limits: the source model decision is not deterministic quality proof
fail-open behavior increases retrieval rather than proving retrieval was necessary
the original prompt contains personal-assistant assumptions and is not portable authority
this mechanism does not solve ranking, memory correctness, write policy, or answer quality
this asset has structural/source evidence; target-context reuse still requires evaluation
evidence_state: STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_EVIDENCE_HIGH; NOT UNIVERSAL LIVE QUALITY PROOF
governance_note: This asset preserves mechanism knowledge, not the Waku Agent. It is not a Platform Capability identity and does not authorize a memory subsystem, gate service, or Platform Core field.
